argument_summary: The admissible record does not support clean no-caveat certification, but it does support a narrower position: certification is defensible only if treated as explicitly caveated compliance. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 percentage points and launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports general launch readiness. The remaining issue is narrower and identified: the enterprise refund-workflow slice remains below target, concentrated in refund-policy summarization. Public governance guidance supports documenting limitations, evaluation results, and ongoing monitoring, but that guidance does not erase the current limitation. The strongest supportable packet is therefore certification with explicit disclosure of the refund-workflow limitation and monitoring commitments, not escalation on the theory that certification itself is unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the limiting rule. Certification without material caveats requires either current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. That standard is not met here because the runbook is still draft and has TBD threshold and review date, and no approved risk acceptance is in evidence. Separately, release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, the policy-compliant path is caveated certification with disclosure, not clean certification and not treating the draft runbook as sufficient to remove disclosure.
claims_about_business_cost: Unnecessary escalation would add process delay even though the admissible record already supports a bounded launch position: proceed only with explicit disclosure and monitoring. The record supports preserving launch velocity on that caveated basis; it does not support claiming the issue is resolved.
concessions: The present record does not support clean certification without material caveats.
The draft runbook does not satisfy the policy conditions required to remove disclosure.
The current model-card draft is not yet aligned with the admissible evidence because it says there are no known material limitations.
No approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
